cues.text: Thirteen.
Consolidation.
Let us bring the main ideas of this session together, in the order we met them.
First, operations.
Operations are what sustain services, keeping them running day after day so that the organisation can rely on them.
Closely linked to this is IT service management, or ITSM, which manages value and service delivery.
It is the discipline that makes sure services actually benefit the organisation and are delivered well.
Next come the frameworks and standards that guide this work.
ITIL provides guidance, a body of recommended practice for managing services.
ISO 20000 is different in an important way: it provides certifiable requirements, meaning an organisation can be formally assessed against it.
And MOF, the Microsoft Operations Framework, supports operational lifecycle management, helping organisations manage operations across the life of a service.
Then we looked at agreements and quality.
Service level agreements, or SLAs, define service expectations, setting out what the customer can expect to receive.
Operational level agreements, or OLAs, coordinate internal support, helping the teams inside the organisation work together so those expectations can be met.
And remember that service quality includes both technical outcomes and perceived outcomes.
A service can perform well on the numbers and still be judged poorly if users experience it badly.
After that, we considered change and projects.
Technical change control protects stability, making sure changes to systems do not cause unplanned disruption.
Organisational change models support adoption, helping people accept and use what has changed.
And project management delivers temporary initiatives, the time-bound pieces of work that introduce new services or improvements.
Finally, identity and access management.
IAM auditing enforces least privilege, so that people hold only the access they need.
By doing this, it reduces privilege creep, which is the gradual build-up of unnecessary access over time.

Taken together: operations and ITSM keep and deliver value, ITIL, ISO 20000 and MOF guide how, SLAs and OLAs set and support expectations, change control and project management handle change, and IAM auditing keeps access under control.
